newsitem.title: UK: Fergie might make court appearance in book case.
newsitem.headline: Fergie might make court appearance in book case.

text.p: The Duchess of York might have to appear in court next month after a judge renewed a temporary injunction on Wednesday stopping a former friend from publishing intimate details about her life in a new book.

The ex-wife of Queen Elizabeth's second son, Prince Andrew, is battling against Allan Starkie who plans to tell all about her relationship with her former "financial adviser" John Bryan in a book entitled "Fergie: Her Secret Life".

While still married to Andrew, the duchess, popularly known as Fergie, was photographed cavorting with Bryan by a swimming pool in the south of France. An infamous picture of Bryan sucking the toe of the topless duchess was published around the world.
The High Court judge, after hearings in private, renewed an injunction granted six weeks ago until October 7, when a trial in open court will begin.
"The Duchess of York has again successfully used the English courts to keep the truth from the British people," publisher Michael O'Mara said after the ruling.
"She is publishing her own version of events, as vetted by the Palace, in a few weeks," he added. "She, and perhaps the Palace as well, have an interest in keeping the truth from the public."
Under the terms of the continuing injunction the duchess must provide security of 500,000 pounds ($780,000) for any damages which might be suffered by the defendants if she loses the case.

The fiery-haired former Sarah Ferguson is writing her own account of her life which is due in book stores later this year, but under her divorce settlement she is barred from speaking about life in the royal family.
"In the words of my counsel...the duchess is a manic self-publicist who only seeks to portray herself in a good light," said O'Mara.
He said he assumed the duchess would give evidence during the case and looked forward to seeing her in court.
